g.text: A visual overview of the Land of the Rising Sun

text.tspan: Japan is an island nation in East Asia, located in the
northwest Pacific Ocean. Known for its unique blend
of ultra-modern technology and deeply rooted traditions,
it comprises four main islands: Hokkaido, Honshu,
Shikoku, and Kyushu.
With a population of approximately 125 million, Japan
is one of the most densely populated countries in the
world. Its capital, Tokyo, is a global financial hub and
the world's most populous metropolitan area.
The country is renowned for its high life expectancy,
advanced infrastructure, and significant cultural exports
ranging from anime and cuisine to automotive engineering.
Japan holds the position of the world's fourth-largest economy by nominal GDP, a testament to its massive industrial
output and technological innovation. Despite recent economic fluctuations and demographic challenges, it remains a
cornerstone of the global market, leading in sectors such as robotics, electronics, and automotive manufacturing.
Japan's nominal GDP in current US dollars has
experienced notable volatility over the past decade.
Peaking around 2019, the figures reflect a combination
of domestic economic policies, global market shifts,
and currency exchange rate fluctuations.
The recent decline from 2021 to 2024 highlights the
impact of a weakening Yen against the US Dollar,
rather than a pure contraction in domestic output.
Understanding these currency dynamics is crucial
when evaluating Japan's true economic health.
Tokyo:
Shibuya Crossing, Senso-ji Temple, Akihabara.
Kyoto:
Fushimi Inari, Kinkaku-ji, Arashiyama Bamboo Grove.
Osaka:
Dotonbori nightlife, Osaka Castle, Universal Studios.
Hiroshima/Miyajima:
Peace Memorial Park, floating Torii gate.
Mt. Fuji/Hakone:
Iconic volcanic views, hot spring resorts.
Hokkaido:
Sapporo Snow Festival, vast national parks, skiing.

svg.text: Sources: World Bank Open Data (GDP), Japan Ministry of Internal Affairs (Population), JNTO. Data as of late 2024.
